messages:
sara.ops: Heads-up — we need to schedule a short maintenance window for control-plane certificate rotation and a db schema migration that touches the routing table. Target window: Thu 2026-04-08 22:00–22:30 UTC (low traffic region). I want to get alignment on customer-facing language and the on-call handoff plan.

mike.oncall: ack. I can take the lead for the actual drain and verification. planning to run the drain at :54 and start migration at :58 to minimize overlap with active requests. Will have rollback steps ready.

amy.support: can we prepare two variants of the customer notice: one short e-mail/blurb and one longer note for customers with dedicated capacity? Also need a quick SLA impact line.

joel.prodcomms: putting together a status page + email template. Draft below — pls comment.

-----STATUS PAGE DRAFT-----
Summary: Brief planned maintenance to rotate control-plane TLS certs and perform a minor routing-table schema upgrade. No customer data will be modified. We expect brief request retries and zero persistent errors.
Start: Thu 2026-04-08 22:00 UTC
End (expected): Thu 2026-04-08 22:30 UTC
Impact: Brief 100–500ms increased latency for in-flight requests during the 2–5 minute drain/migration window. Applications using Dedicated capacity may observe up to 1% transient request failures; automatic retries recommended.
Customer guidance: No action required for most customers. If you have pinned model versions or strict SLOs and run dedicated clusters, consider rescheduling non-critical heavy batch jobs to outside the window.
Contacts: support@redwood.ai and status.redwood.ai
-----END DRAFT-----

amy.support: looks good. suggest adding an explicit "when we'll follow up" line and a TL;DR for the email.

joel.prodcomms: updated draft with follow-up line and TL;DR. Email copy below — short variant first.

-----EMAIL (SHORT)-----
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief service update on Thu Apr 8
Hi — we will perform a brief maintenance window on Thu 2026-04-08 22:00–22:30 UTC to rotate control-plane certificates and apply a small routing-table upgrade. Most customers will not see any disruption; you may see brief retries or slightly higher latency for a few minutes. We will post updates on status.redwood.ai and follow up when complete.
If you are on Dedicated and rely on pinned throughput/SLOs, please review queued jobs. Contact support@redwood.ai if you expect critical impact.
-----END EMAIL-----

mike.oncall: nice. Operational checklist for on-call:
1) preflight health checks and traffic snapshot (run `curl -s https://internal-metrics/api/traffic | jq .`)
2) disable autoscale for affected pools
3) drain set A, confirm kv cache flush 
4) run migration script: `./scripts/migrate-routing.sh --dry-run` then `--apply`
5) verify tail logs for errors and re-enable autoscale
6) post status page update and send completion email

incident-bot: Reminder from incident-scheduler: maintenance window scheduled Thu 2026-04-08 22:00 UTC. 24h notice sent. Pager escalation unchanged.

ryan-eng: quick timezone note — APAC customers see that on Fri morning local time. Joel, can we include a localized time snippet in the email? e.g., 22:00 UTC / Fri 06:00 JST.

joel.prodcomms: yep will add localized times for UTC, PDT, CET, JST and a line: "All times shown in UTC; your local time is shown for convenience."

amy.support: routing for high-touch customers: I'll prepare tailored snippets (we have a list of Dedicated customers impacted if any). We'll send targeted emails to them 12h prior.

sara.ops: one more ask — add a short internal playbook for oncall handoff in the channel at least 30m before start. Who's on the next shift after Mike?

mike.oncall: ryan will be the handback; I'll post a quick runbook when the drain starts.

ryan-eng: roger. I can take the post-maint verification and customer follow-ups. Please include me on the status page edit permissions.

joel.prodcomms: final status page + email templates attached here (copy/paste). Also adding a quick internal msg for support & sales.

-----INTERNAL COMMUNICATION (support/sales)-----
Heads up — short maintenance Thu 2026-04-08 22:00–22:30 UTC. Expected impact: transient latency + <1% retryable errors for Dedicated. No action required for most customers. If asked by customers, escalate to amy.support (support@redwood.ai). We'll send targeted notices to high-touch accounts 12h prior.
-----END INTERNAL-----

amy.support: can we include a canned troubleshooting snippet for support agents? e.g., 
`If a customer reports request failures, first check status.redwood.ai; then verify request id in logs: 
  1) grep request id in gateway logs
  2) check model-serving pool health
  3) escalate to oncall if errors persist`

mike.oncall: fine with that. One more operational change: due to a staging inconsistency we will do a two-phase rollout (A then B) to reduce impact. Details in runbook.

incident-bot: maintenance window updated: two-phase rollout enabled. New subwindow plan: A 22:00–22:10 UTC, B 22:10–22:25 UTC.

sara.ops: thanks. small change to the templates to reflect phased rollout. Joel, please update the customer-facing text to say "phased rollout, brief retries possible during each phase".

joel.prodcomms: updated; pushing to status page and queued email. I'll publish the status-page "maintenance scheduled" entry now and mark "We will update at start and at completion."

(many reactions: :thumbsup:, :eyes:)

---POST-MAINTENANCE FOLLOW-UP (later same thread)---

mike.oncall: POST-MAINT: rotation + migration completed. Phase A and B succeeded. Observed a 3 minute tail where retry rate peaked at 0.9% then returned to baseline. No rollback required.

incident-bot: Status update: Completed — all systems nominal. Status page incident entry updated to 'Resolved'.

amy.support: I've sent the completion email to targeted high-touch accounts and the general notice. Support queue saw 4 tickets related to transient timeouts; all resolved.

ryan-eng: I'll run post-maint validation script and confirm perf histograms by EOD.

joel.prodcomms: Published post-maint blog + short follow-up note on status page with timeline and what we observed. Copy for records: 
"Summary: Certificates rotated and routing-table migration applied. No data loss. A transient spike in retries up to 0.9% was observed during the tail of the migration. We will keep monitoring and will alert if any regression appears"

sara.ops: Great work team. Closing thread — please drop any follow-ups here.
